paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Section V experimental setup and Fig. 5 / Fig. 6 (MTTF results)
scenario.description: Simulated 8x8 NoC-based many-core system (16nm, 109 mm^2 squared floorplan, TDP 90 W) running 25 randomly selected multi-threaded PARSEC applications under the proposed thermal-cycling-aware resource manager (mapping, scheduling, DPM) compared with a nominal baseline, MOC, and reliability-aware mapping. The reported observable is per-core thermal-cycling MTTF (years), summarized as MIN, STD and AVG. Only total chip area and TDP are published; no per-block coordinates, dimensions or per-block power values are given.
scenario.architecture: 8x8 homogeneous mesh NoC many-core, Niagara2-like SPARC cores, private L1 and distributed shared L2, four memory controllers, per-core DVFS and PCPG, per-core temperature sensors
scenario.workload: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmarks, 25 randomly selected application executions issued at runtime
scenario.operating_point: TDP 90 W, 16nm, chip area 109 mm^2; thermal cycling model EaTC=0.42 eV, b=2.35, Tth=1 C, A_TC fitted for MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C, 1 hour, m=10; temperature sampling about 1 s

original_setup.solver: Noculator (shared-memory NoC-based many-core simulator built on Intel PIN) with McPAT/Lumos power and scaling parameters, and HotSpot steady-state thermal model integrated; thermal-cycling reliability computed via rainflow counting, Miner's rule and Coffin-Manson (Eqs. 1-3) (PDF p.2, p.5)
original_setup.optimizer: Heuristic reliability-aware runtime resource management: RAF affinity-based mapping extending MapPro (Algorithm 2), temperature-deviation-sorted round-robin thread scheduling (Algorithm 3), and DPM extending MOC with a thermal-cycling metric avgAmplitude x maxT (PDF p.3-5)
original_setup.controller: Global feedback controller with reliability analysis unit (about 1 s sampling, 1-2 h long-term period), reliability-aware mapping, thread scheduling (few ms period), and DPM with PID stage plus multi-objective control of per-core DVFS and PCPG under 90 W TDP (PDF p.3-5)
original_setup.benchmark: 8x8 homogeneous many-core (Niagara2/SPARC cores, 16nm, 109 mm^2, TDP 90 W) running 25 randomly selected multi-threaded PARSEC application executions, compared against nominal baseline, MOC and reliability-aware mapping [2] (PDF p.5)

thermal_observable.location: Per core of the 8x8 many-core; Fig. 5 per-core MTTF snapshot and Fig. 6 summary (MIN, STD, AVG); no numeric values are given in the text, only relative improvements (min MTTF +54%, +51%, +39%; avg +40%, +21%, +20% vs baseline, MOC, RA-mapping)
thermal_observable.aggregation: Per-core MTTF_TC from rainflow cycles and Miner's rule over the run; summarized as minimum, standard deviation and average across cores after 25 application executions

physical_mismatches.reason: The study is a system-level reliability and resource-management evaluation: the observable is thermal-cycling MTTF (years), not a steady-state temperature field, so it cannot be compared directly to a steady 2D thermal solve.

Transient, workload-driven dynamics are essential (temperature traces sampled about 1 s, rainflow cycle extraction, ms-scale scheduling, 1-2 h control epochs, random application arrivals); a single-row steady power trace cannot reproduce the thermal-cycling amplitude and frequency.
The controller (PID plus multi-objective DPM, mapping unit, scheduler, PCPG and DVFS) and the heuristic optimizer are not representable in a static placement or thermal solve.
Original thermal solver is HotSpot steady-state with unspecified package, cooling and material parameters; the cooling and interposer are not described, and no 3D stacking is involved.

No per-core or per-block geometry (x, y, width, height) and no per-block power are published; only total chip area 109 mm^2, an 8x8 squared floorplan and a 90 W TDP, so splitting power would require an unpublished rule.
Reliability results (MTTF fitted so MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C) depend on the Coffin-Manson model parameters, which the Studio does not model.

Per-core or per-block power values and power time series (only 90 W TDP total given)

Linked code, data, configuration or repository assets (artifact search found no links; packet assets list is empty)
Fitted A_TC constant value and PARSEC application list/mix and arrival sequence
Selected ATPlace2.5D or RLPlanner Ascend910 configuration files (not supplied and not applicable to this paper)
